grade.basis: Complete four-part score, notation PDF pages 5–8: first cello carries sustained upper-register tenor/treble-clef melody, chromatic shifts, exposed soft attacks and occasional quick ornamental figures; other parts include chromatic running accompaniment and chords. Slow quarter=60–69 limits velocity demand. Advanced tonal control and secure shifting determine the grade; no separate ensemble uplift.
grade.rawCharacter: Intimate, devotional, sustained lyricism with chromatic expression.

findings.finding: Sibley primary record identifies Preghiere for four cellos, Op.27 No.3. Complete source 91745 reviewed locally, with musical notation on PDF pages 5–8.

grade.basis: Correct Dance No.2 opening (sample 3 lower system) and substantial internal passage mm.66–77 (sample 4), together with whole-work publisher technical description. Upper melody reaches treble-clef solo register with chromatic shifting, exposed sustained tones and short irregular ornamental groups; second bass has rhythmic figures and upper-register entries. Lower parts supply repeated pizzicato chords and reggae pulse. Quarter approximately 76 moderates velocity. Advanced register control outweighs the catalogue intermediate label; no ensemble uplift. Advisory estimate approximately one level uncertain; excerpts do not certify every bar.
grade.rawCharacter: Playful reggae groove with singing solo-register melody and colorful articulation.

findings.finding: Cached publisher product body distinguishes Dance No.2 reggae accompaniment in basses 3–4 and solo-register melody in basses 1–2; upper parts frequently use solo register, lower parts stay at or below third position with some double stops.
Actual Dance No.2 internal score page 13, mm.66–77, reviewed; samples 1–2 belong to Dance No.1 and were excluded from grading.

grade.basis: Complete first-cello part reviewed through theme, eleven variations and coda (seven PDF pages including cover). Repeated treble/tenor-clef thumb-position passagework, wide arpeggios and rapid register changes, fast continuous spiccato semiquavers in Variation VIII at quarter=152, ornamental figures, pizzicato chords and sustained exposed high melody make the lead part diploma-level. Whole-work edition context corroborates unequal parts and thumb-position writing in upper three voices. No additional ensemble uplift. Advisory estimate about one level uncertain because remaining parts were not available for notation inspection; complete commercially published four-part set suffices as the edition.
grade.rawCharacter: Romantic concert variations, lyrical theme with increasingly agile, brilliant and strongly articulated contrasts.

findings.finding: Primary scanned IMC 1764 first-cello part, reprinting Breitkopf plate 17434, reviewed completely; includes all eleven variations and coda.

Specialist commercial edition description identifies unequal parts: cellos I–III include thumb position and treble clef; IV remains in bass clef with chords and counting challenges; set of parts, no score.
Primary IMC catalogue identifies edition 1764 in the four-cello repertoire, corroborating the commercial complete ensemble edition.
